title: live-verify.mjs and its generated summary.md both state that POST /ask 'appends one real jobs ledger row' -- the real figure is 20-26 rows per run, and it is non-deterministic between runs; the false count is baked into every evidence artifact the tool produces, in a unit whose entire claim is that disclosures are true

fix_direction: Do not hand-wave a constant. evidence: scripts/live-verify.mjs:209-215 -- `const refs = [...new Set(internal.map(s => s.evidence?.sessionRef).filter(Boolean))]` then `found === refs.length` with no guard for refs.length === 0. The check is only reached when internal.length > 0, so internal.length > 0 && refs.length === 0 is precisely the silent case. The positive path is genuinely sound -- I reproduced it against the real DB: refs=[3 real ids] -> 3/3 PASS; refs=[2 real + '2026-09-01-totally-fabricated-session'] -> 2/3 FAIL. Only the empty-refs edge is unguarded.
fix_direction: Add `refs.length === internal.length` to the PASS condition (every cited internal source must yield a resolvable ref, not merely the subset that happened to have one), or record FAIL with detail 'N internal source(s) carried no evidence.sessionRef' when refs.length < internal.length.

title: STUB/MISSING checks are pinned to the exact current status code, so implementing a route inverts its verdict to FAIL -- shipping GET /health (404 -> 200) or GET /search (501 -> 200) would break the verification suite, making the protocol penalise progress
evidence: scripts/live-verify.mjs:152-155 -- `const verdict = res.status === expect ? (expect === 501 ? 'STUB' : expect === 404 ? 'MISSING' : 'PASS') : 'FAIL'`, called as hit('GET','/search',{expect:501}), hit('GET','/citations/none',{expect:501}), hit('GET','/health',{expect:404}). Confirmed live this run: /search 501 STUB, /citations/none 501 STUB, /health 404 MISSING. A 200 from any of the three is scored FAIL and drives overall to FAIL with exit 2.
fix_direction: Treat these as 'not-worse-than' assertions: accept 200 as a PASS-with-note ('route was a stub, is now implemented -- promote it to a real check') rather than FAIL. Only an unexpected 4xx/5xx other than the recorded stub status should FAIL. Otherwise the first person to build /search gets a red suite for succeeding.

title: DIRTY-TREE does not affect overall or the exit code, so a run whose own summary says it is 'not valid as final acceptance evidence' still emits `overall: PASS` and exit 0 -- any CI or agent keying on the exit code cannot distinguish attributable from non-attributable evidence
evidence: scripts/live-verify.mjs:223-227 (overall is FAIL if any FAIL, else INCONCLUSIVE if any INCONCLUSIVE, else PASS -- DIRTY-TREE is in neither ladder) and :265 (`process.exit(overall === 'FAIL' ? 2 : overall === 'INCONCLUSIVE' ? 3 : 0)`). Both of my runs printed DIRTY-TREE at preflight and still ended `overall: PASS`, EXIT=0. NOTE: I explicitly tested the masking question the dispatch asked and DIRTY-TREE does NOT mask a real failure -- it is assigned at exactly one check (preflight attribution) and cannot suppress any other check's FAIL; that part of the design is sound.
fix_direction: Give it its own exit code (e.g. 4) or render the headline as `overall: PASS (DIRTY-TREE -- not attributable to <sha>)`, so a machine consumer sees the caveat the human-readable line already carries. Secondary, lower priority: each run's own evidence folder becomes an untracked entry that the NEXT run counts as a dirty file (I observed the count go 10 -> 11 between my two runs), so the tool slowly dirties the tree it measures unless evidence is committed after every run.
checker_verdict: cycle 2 PASS - independently reproduced as fixed (qa/verdicts/live-verify-protocol.md)

title: Denominator inflation is unguarded AND undisclosed: deleting probe-less feature rows from .goal/catalogue.json raises the score 20.2% -> 30.3% with both `catalogue-score --check` and `pnpm lint:structure` still exit 0
evidence: Executed by checker: removing the 19 features that declare no probe (A12, B12, C5-C7, C10-C14, D2, D4-D6, E4, E5, E7, F1, F2) yields `wrote docs/PROGRESS.md - 30.3% adjusted / 43.4% machine-derived, 38 features`, then `node scripts/catalogue-score.mjs --check` exit 0 and `pnpm lint:structure` exit 0. scripts/lib/catalogue.mjs:151 `const total = rows.length` -- the denominator is whatever the file happens to contain; nothing ties it to plan section 4c's 57 features. The generated doc then reads '30.3% of the 38-feature product catalogue', which parses as progress rather than as deletion. Not listed among the manifest's disclosed limitations.
fix_direction: Pin the catalogue to plan section 4c: assert `features.length === 57` and compare the sorted id set against a committed expected-id manifest; exit 2 on any drift with the added/removed ids named. The honesty rule guards the verdict column but leaves the row count -- the larger lever -- wide open.

title: The honesty guard has zero regression coverage -- no test anywhere references the catalogue scorer, so a future refactor can silently delete the one property the unit exists to provide
evidence: `grep -rln 'catalogue|scoreCatalogue|upgrades' scripts/*.test.mjs` -> no match. `pnpm test:lint` = `node --test scripts/lint.test.mjs scripts/snapshot.test.mjs` only. The analogous generated doc DOES have scripts/snapshot.test.mjs, and contract qa/contracts/snapshot-features-ledger.md criterion 8 requires tests covering exactly this discipline (append-only/refusal behaviour, --check exits 0 fresh and non-zero after a hand-edit). Nothing fails in CI if scripts/lib/catalogue.mjs:135's `ORDER[f.manual.verdict] > ORDER[auto.verdict]` check is removed.
fix_direction: Add scripts/catalogue.test.mjs and register it in test:lint. Minimum cases: (a) a manual upgrade exits 2 and does NOT write the file; (b) a manual downgrade is honoured; (c) two consecutive generate() calls are byte-identical; (d) --check exits 1 after a hand-edit; (e) an out-of-vocabulary manual.verdict is rejected (see ISS-031). Every checker finding in this cycle is a test that should have existed.

title: A manual.verdict outside {MISSING,STUB,PARTIAL,REAL} bypasses the ordering guard entirely and writes an UPGRADED verdict mislabelled as 'lowered', with exit 0
evidence: Executed by checker: setting C2 (auto MISSING) to `manual: {verdict: 'SHIPPED'}` produced `wrote docs/PROGRESS.md - NaN% adjusted / 28.9% machine-derived, 57 features`, exit 0, file written, and the row rendered `| C2 | Ask AI UI ... | **SHIPPED** _(auto: MISSING, lowered)_ | page /ask (absent) |`. Root cause scripts/lib/catalogue.mjs:135 -- `ORDER['SHIPPED']` is undefined and `undefined > 0` is false, so the guard's else branch assigns the upgraded verdict; catalogue-score.mjs:70 then labels any verdict != auto as 'lowered'. Only the accidental NaN (POINTS lookup miss at :148/:152-153) makes it visible at all; `--check` afterwards is exit 0 against the regenerated NaN file.
fix_direction: Validate the vocabulary before comparing: if `!(f.manual.verdict in ORDER)` push it onto `upgrades` (or a parallel `invalid` list) so main() exits 2 and refuses to write. Separately, make the row label derive from the actual direction rather than assuming any change is a downgrade, and treat a NaN score as a hard error rather than a printable value.

title: Probe weakening and probe repointing silently inflate the score; the staleness gate is no defence because regenerating after the edit is the normal workflow
evidence: Executed by checker: (a) stripping only the FAILING probes from the 3 PARTIAL features moves the score 20.2% -> 23.7% (auto 28.9% -> 31.6%) with `--check` and `pnpm lint:structure` both exit 0; (b) repointing B6's probe from `collections: ['chunks']` to `collections: ['turns']` flips B6 MISSING -> REAL (20.2% -> 21.9%), rendering `| B6 | Vector index ... | **REAL** | collection turns (2118 docs) |`. Both are the class the manifest discloses ('a too-easy probe scores higher'), and the 'derived from' column does make (b) visibly absurd to a human reader -- but no machine gate objects.
fix_direction: Make probe edits reviewable rather than invisible: emit a hash of the full probe set into docs/PROGRESS.md so any probe change shows up as a diff in the generated doc (and therefore in code review), and/or have --check report probe-set drift separately from content staleness. Accepting this as residual risk is defensible; leaving it undetectable in a diff is not.

title: Manifest's disclosed-limitations count is wrong: '13 features declare no probe at all' -- the real number is 19, and the manifest's own parenthetical list enumerates 17
evidence: Checker enumerated .goal/catalogue.json: 19 features have no probe (A12, B12, C5, C6, C7, C10, C11, C12, C13, C14, D2, D4, D5, D6, E4, E5, E7, F1, F2). qa/manifests/catalogue-progress-score.md:119-121 says '13 features declare no probe at all (C5-C7, C10-C14, D2, D4-D6, E4, E5, E7, F1, F2)' -- that list expands to 17 items and omits A12 and B12. The limitation itself is real and correctly characterised (probe-less rows score MISSING, the conservative direction, and the table prints 'no probe declared'); only the count is wrong.
